signals.signal: Bank's own machine-readable branch/ATM locator feed, pulled 27/08/2026, returns 520 places: 417 ATM entries and 103 branches. Splitting the ATMs by the services the bank itself tags on each device: 206 are full multifunction units (RSD deposit + RSD dispense + EUR cash in/out + balance + contactless), 35 do RSD deposit and dispense but no EUR, 51 are deposit-only (tagged solely 'Uplata dinara'), and 125 are cash-out-only (dispense + balance + contactless, no deposit). So 292 of 417 devices (70%) take cash in and 125 are dispense-only.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — locations map JSON feed (maps.viewport.json)
signals.implies: 125 dispense-only ATMs are the addressable white space for cash recycler upgrades/replacement; the 206 EUR-capable multifunction units prove the bank already buys FX-capable recycling hardware and will keep buying. Printec: cash automation/recyclers, ATM managed services, ATM software.
signals.likelihood: High — the bank states in its own 2025 annual report that it is actively expanding the multifunction fleet
signals.followup: Re-pull this same JSON monthly; a change in the 292/125 split is itself the signal. Identify the hardware vendor behind the 206 EUR-capable units (NCR Atleos vs Diebold Nixdorf) before pitching.

signals.signal: Same locator feed shows 36 of the bank's 103 branches are tagged 'Bezgotovinska filijala' (cashless branch, i.e. no cash handled over the counter). Only 54 branches have a teller desk open until 13:00 and just 13 have a full-day teller desk; 98 of the 103 branches carry an in-branch 'Visenamenski uredaj' (multifunction device) and 6 sites are tagged 'Cash HUB'.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — locations map JSON feed (maps.viewport.json)
signals.implies: 35% of the branch network already runs with zero counter cash and the rest is being pushed to half-day tellering — meaning every remaining cash flow has to land on a machine. This is the classic branch-cash-migration project. Printec: in-branch teller cash recyclers, self-service zones, cash-hub/CIT optimisation, managed services.
signals.likelihood: High — cashless-branch share is disclosed as a current state, not a plan
signals.followup: Map the 6 'Cash HUB' sites and the 36 cashless branches; ask whether the 98 in-branch multifunction devices are the same platform as the lobby ATMs or a separate teller-assist device.

signals.signal: The locator tags two named merchant cash-deposit ('uplata pazara' = paying in the day's takings) device brands inside branches: 'Kuan uredaj za uplatu pazara' at 34 branches and 'Livix uredaj za uplatu pazara' at 14 branches — i.e. 48 named third-party smart-safe/deposit terminals are already installed in the network.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — locations map JSON feed (maps.viewport.json)
signals.implies: Named competitor incumbency in the merchant cash-in niche and a proven willingness to run two vendors in parallel — so it is a contestable, multi-vendor estate rather than a locked single-source account. Printec: cash automation / smart safes for retail merchants, plus the managed-service wrap.
signals.likelihood: Medium — replacement/expansion cycle rather than a greenfield tender
signals.followup: Confirm who supplies and services 'Kuan' and 'Livix' units in Serbia and on what contract term; the 34/14 split suggests one vendor is winning the rollout.

signals.signal: 2025 Annual Report, retail chapter: 'Posebna paznja posvecena je daljoj digitalnoj transformaciji fizicke mreze. Sirenje i unapredjivanje mreze visenamenskih uredjaja i uredjaja za uplatu pazara dostupnih 24/7' — the bank states it is expanding and upgrading its network of multifunction devices and merchant cash-takings deposit devices available 24/7, explicitly to take load off branch operations.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd — Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf)
signals.implies: An expressed, board-level commitment to grow the self-service cash estate — the demand driver behind the locator numbers. Printec: recyclers, self-service, managed services.
signals.followup: Ask for the 2026 capex line for self-service devices; check the H1-2026 statements for a step-up in property/equipment additions.

signals.signal: 2025 Annual Report, Premium Banking: 97% of Premium clients' cash transactions are carried out on multifunction devices, 93% of the Premium client base interacts with the bank remotely and 92% of sales to that segment are done remotely; total Premium client base up 13.2% year on year.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd — Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf)
signals.implies: The bank has quantified proof that self-service absorbs essentially all cash demand in its most valuable segment — the internal business case for pushing the same model to mass retail is already written. Printec: recyclers, self-service zones, video-teller/assisted-service.
signals.followup: Get the equivalent self-service share for mass retail — the gap between that and 97% is the sizing of the next rollout.

signals.signal: 2025 Annual Report, retail digital: active digital banking users reached 600,000 and over 100,000 new clients were acquired through digital channels during 2025; all key retail products are stated to be fully digitalised, with fully online RSD account opening and FX account opening via 'iRacun' in under 20 minutes, and 'Biznis iRacun' opening a company current/FX account fully online in under 30 minutes.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd — Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf)
signals.implies: iRacun is a live, at-scale remote onboarding funnel — 100k+ digital acquisitions a year — which means continuous demand for identity proofing, liveness/document checks, sanctions and AML screening at onboarding. Printec: digital onboarding/eKYC, AML/compliance, transaction monitoring.
signals.followup: Identify the incumbent eKYC/video-identification vendor behind iRacun and whether the contract is up for renewal; confirm whether NBS video-identification rules require an upgrade.

signals.signal: 2025 Annual Report, corporate: 36% of active corporate clients completed the KYC (know-your-customer) process digitally via the iPortal platform with electronic signatures, and the bank states full digitalisation of corporate onboarding was planned for Q1 2026. iPortal users rose from 727 (Q1 2024) to 2,085 (Q4 2025), 56% of active corporate clients.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd — Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf)
signals.implies: A dated 2026 milestone for corporate eKYC with 64% of the base still to migrate. Corporate KYC is harder than retail (UBO discovery, corporate registry lookups, periodic review) and is exactly where compliance tooling gets bought. Printec: digital onboarding/eKYC, AML/compliance.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the Q1-2026 target date has passed; verify whether it landed
signals.followup: Verify whether full corporate digital onboarding actually went live in Q1 2026 — a slip is a sales opening, a hit is a reference for periodic-review automation.

signals.signal: 2025 Annual Report, cards/acquiring: card acceptance at POS terminals grew 32% year on year and e-commerce acceptance 44%; the RaiPOS tap-to-phone app (a phone used as a POS terminal) grew over 90% year on year. The bank describes itself as one of the market leaders in acceptance, standing out on acceptance-network growth.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd — Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf)
signals.implies: An acquiring book growing 30%+ needs terminal estate, terminal management, certification and PCI/HSM capacity to match — and tap-to-phone growth of 90% adds a software-attestation and key-management load. Printec: POS/acquiring, terminal managed services, HSM/security.
signals.followup: Get the actual installed POS terminal count and the terminal-management/estate vendor; check NBS Serbia POS statistics for the bank's share.

signals.signal: RBI Group Q2-2026 databook, sheet 'SEE-RS': Raiffeisen Serbia had 1,175,109 customers at 30/06/2026, up 6.50% from 1,103,436 at 30/06/2025 (31/12/2025: 1,137,070; 31/12/2024: 1,068,469). The bank is therefore already past one million clients and adding roughly 70,000 net customers a year.
signals.source_name: RBI — Q2/2026 Results Internet databook (.xlsm), sheet SEE-RS
signals.implies: Resolves the '1m-client target' question: the milestone is behind them, not ahead. The live story is absorbing +70k clients a year on a network that is not growing — which lands squarely on self-service capacity, digital onboarding throughput and AML screening volume. Printec: eKYC, self-service, transaction monitoring.
signals.followup: Ask whether a public '1.5 million clients' or similar target has replaced the 1m goal; check the next RBI quarterly databook for the run-rate.

signals.signal: Same RBI Q2-2026 databook, SEE-RS: business outlets 104 at 30/06/2026 (105 a year earlier, 104 at 31/12/2025) and employees 2,149 (2,207 a year earlier, -2.6%). Set against customers +6.5%, loans to customers EUR 3,765.1m (+17.3% y/y) and deposits EUR 5,556.0m (+10.6% y/y) on total assets of EUR 7,035.7m (+9.4%).
signals.source_name: RBI — Q2/2026 Results Internet databook (.xlsm), sheet SEE-RS
signals.implies: A flat branch count and a shrinking headcount carrying a book that is growing 10-17% — the classic pre-condition for a self-service and automation buy. Every extra transaction has to go somewhere other than a teller. Printec: recyclers, self-service, managed services, in-branch automation.
signals.followup: Ask what transactions-per-branch and transactions-per-FTE look like; those two ratios are the pitch.

signals.signal: Same RBI Q2-2026 databook, SEE-RS: cost/income ratio 30.57% for H1-2026 (H1-2025 29.24%), return on equity after tax 32.52%, profit after tax EUR 130.8m (+6.3% y/y). By RBI's own country tables this is the most cost-efficient unit in the group, against a group cost/income ratio of 52.2%.
signals.source_name: RBI — Q2/2026 Results Internet databook (.xlsm), sheet SEE-RS; RBI Q2/2026 Report
signals.implies: Two-sided: the bank has the profitability to fund automation capex, but the CIR ticked UP 1.3pp year on year — the first deterioration in a while, which is exactly the trigger that makes a cost-per-transaction argument land. Printec: cash automation and managed services sold on cost-to-serve.
signals.likelihood: Medium — capex decisions sit with RBI Vienna as well as Belgrade
signals.followup: Watch Q3-2026 CIR; a second consecutive rise sharpens the window. Confirm whether self-service capex is approved locally or in Vienna.

signals.signal: Same RBI Q2-2026 databook, SEE-RS: a 'Resolution fund' charge of EUR 4.58m appears for H1-2026 against EUR 0 in every prior period back to 2024; RBI's Q2-2026 presentation shows Serbia resolution-fund cost of EUR 0m in FY2025, EUR 4m in 1-6/2026 and EUR 8m expected for FY2026. Deposit insurance fees fell to EUR 4.50m (H1-2025 EUR 6.98m).
signals.source_name: RBI — Q2/2026 Results Internet databook (.xlsm), sheet SEE-RS, and RBI Q2/2026 results presentation
signals.implies: A brand-new Serbian bank resolution levy landing in 2026 at roughly EUR 8m a year for this bank alone. New resolution regimes bring recovery-and-resolution data and reporting obligations, and they squeeze the cost base — both push automation and compliance-reporting spend. Printec: AML/compliance and regulatory reporting; indirect pressure on cost-to-serve.
signals.likelihood: High — the charge is already booked
signals.followup: Trace the enabling NBS/Serbian law behind the 2026 resolution fund and check what reporting/data obligations it creates for banks.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (market context for Raiffeisen Serbia)
signals.signal: NBS acceptance-network statistics updated 19/08/2026: Serbia had 3,412 ATMs and 195,121 POS terminals at the end of Q2-2026, up from 3,336 ATMs / 187,957 POS at Q1-2026 and 3,265 ATMs / 184,656 POS at 31/12/2025. Virtual points of sale reached 6,278. The national ATM fleet therefore grew by 147 machines (+4.5%) in the first half of 2026 and POS by 10,465 (+5.7%).
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia — Acceptance network statistics (prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)
signals.implies: Serbia is one of the few European markets where the ATM estate is still GROWING, and POS is compounding at ~6% a half-year. Against that, Raiffeisen's 417 ATM entries are about 12% of the national fleet. A growing fleet means new-build and upgrade demand rather than decommissioning. Printec: ATM/self-service, recyclers, POS/acquiring, managed services.
signals.followup: Pull the Q3-2026 update (NBS refreshes roughly quarterly) and break the 147-machine increase down by bank if NBS or the banks' locators allow.

signals.signal: Bank's own SEPA explainer: from 05/05/2026 Serbia is inside SEPA (the Single Euro Payments Area). Raiffeisen banka states that in this phase it joins only the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) scheme, as do all banks in Serbia, that all Serbian banks are INDIRECT SEPA participants, and that Raiffeisen participates through its parent Raiffeisen Bank International AG in Austria as the direct participant. SCT does not run 24/7 and the cut-off for SEPA FX orders is 13:00, the same as SWIFT. The page also notes Bosnia and Herzegovina is announced as a new SEPA country from 2027.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — 'SEPA - pitanja i odgovori' (SEPA Q&A)
signals.implies: Serbia's SEPA entry is live but deliberately minimal — SCT only, indirect, batch cycles, 13:00 cut-off. The two schemes NOT yet taken (SEPA Instant Credit Transfer, 10-second settlement, and SEPA Direct Debit) are the obvious next build, and each brings 24/7 payment processing, real-time sanctions and fraud screening, and IBAN/name verification obligations. Printec: transaction monitoring, AML/compliance, payments-adjacent managed services.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — SCT Inst and SDD are the standard next steps once a market is admitted
signals.followup: Track when Serbian banks move to SCT Inst and SDD, and whether NBS sets a dated deadline; that date is the buying trigger. Also watch the BiH 2027 SEPA date as a regional follow-on.

signals.signal: On 24/08/2026 the bank announced six Global Finance 'World's Best Corporate Digital Bank Awards 2026' wins for Serbia, including best corporate digital bank, best SME digital banking platform, most innovative digital bank, best online portal and user experience, and best online currency-conversion and CASH MANAGEMENT services. Executive Board member Tanja Glisin attributes this to the iPortal corporate platform. The bank separately took a PC Press Top 50 'Digital Banking Leader' special award on 13/02/2026.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — press release, six Global Finance awards
signals.implies: Freshest in-window disclosure and a direct reference to corporate CASH MANAGEMENT as a competitive strength — the same buyer who owns cash management owns the merchant cash-deposit device estate ('uplata pazara' terminals). That is the warmest door for Printec's cash-automation and smart-safe proposition.
signals.followup: Route a cash-automation approach through the corporate/cash-management owner (Executive Board member for corporate banking) rather than retail operations.

signals.signal: RBI Q2-2026 databook, SEE-RS cost lines for H1-2026 vs H1-2025: staff expenses EUR 36.05m (+11.3%), other administrative expenses EUR 21.92m (+11.1%), but depreciation only EUR 10.02m (+1.5%). Total general administrative expenses EUR 67.99m (+9.7%).
signals.source_name: RBI — Q2/2026 Results Internet databook (.xlsm), sheet SEE-RS
signals.implies: Opex is rising 11% while the depreciation charge — the proxy for capitalised hardware already on the books — is flat. Either the self-service expansion the annual report describes is small in euro terms, or it is being consumed as a service rather than bought as capex. Either reading favours an as-a-service / managed-services commercial model over an outright hardware sale. Printec: managed services, device-as-a-service.
signals.likelihood: Medium — an inference from cost lines, not a stated procurement policy
signals.followup: Confirm directly whether Raiffeisen Serbia buys or leases its self-service estate, and whether device servicing is already outsourced and to whom.

signals.signal: The bank published repeated retail fraud warnings during 2026, including a WhatsApp account-takeover scam that hijacks the victim's account and then solicits transfers from their contact list, with the fraudster's account number supplied in the message (published 13/02/2026), plus a separate compromised-phone payment-request scam.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — security notice, WhatsApp vote/loan fraud
signals.implies: Authorised-push-payment fraud — where the genuine customer is tricked into sending the money — is the live threat, and it is precisely what static rules miss. Combined with SEPA entry and a 600k-strong digital base, this argues for behavioural transaction monitoring and beneficiary-account risk scoring. Printec: transaction monitoring, AML/compliance.
signals.followup: Ask whether the bank runs real-time outbound-payment fraud scoring or only card-side monitoring; check for any NBS rule on APP-fraud reimbursement.

signals.signal: NEGATIVE FINDING / baseline correction: the terms 'Bank Yourself' and 'x-core' appear NOWHERE in Raiffeisen banka Serbia's own materials checked this run — not in the 349-URL sitemap, the 2025 Annual Report, the 31/12/2025 Pillar-3 'Podaci i informacije o banci' disclosure, the locator feed, or the Serbian and English self-service pages. The domain bankyourself.rs does not resolve. The bank's own name for its self-service proposition is 'Visenamenski bankomati / visenamenski uredjaji' (multifunction ATMs / multifunction devices).
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia — sitemap.xml, Annual Report 2025, multifunction-ATM pages (searched)
signals.implies: The 'x-core incumbency (Bank Yourself)' brief item could not be corroborated from any primary source. Do not carry it forward as fact, and do not build a displacement pitch on it. Use 'visenamenski uredjaji' as the bank's own vocabulary when approaching them.
signals.likelihood: n/a — this is a correction, not a forecast
signals.followup: Ask the Orchestrator for the original source of the 'x-core / Bank Yourself' claim. If it came from an aggregator or a vendor press release, it needs primary confirmation or retirement. Possible confusion with a different bank or a different market.

coverage_notes:
Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-27). Target: Raiffeisen banka a.d. Beograd (Serbia), RBI Group SEE unit.

WHAT WAS SEARCHED, primary-first:
1. Bank's own site (raiffeisenbank.rs) — pulled and parsed sitemap.xml (349 URLs), the Serbian and English multifunction-ATM pages, the locations page, the 2026 news index and seven individual 2026 press/security items, the reports index (/sr/common/izvestaji.html) and the about page.
2. THE KEY FIND — the bank's AEM locations map exposes a machine-readable JSON feed at
   /sr/stanovnistvo/lokacije/_jcr_content/root/container/map_493090990.maps.viewport.json
   (661 KB, 319 location groups, 520 places, each with a bank-authored service list). This is the Serbian equivalent of the aikbank.rs/data/maps-formated.json route noted in the baseline and it is now the highest-value recurring pull for this bank. It yields the ATM deposit/dispense split, the cashless-branch count, teller-hour coverage, Cash HUB sites, and two NAMED third-party merchant cash-deposit device brands (Kuan, Livix) that the baseline had never seen.
3. Bank's Annual Report 2025 (AR_2025_Final.pdf, bilingual SR/EN, 768k chars extracted locally with pdfminer) and the 31/12/2025 Pillar-3 'Podaci i informacije o banci'. Quarterly unaudited H1-2026 statements confirmed published (balance sheet, P&L, cash flow, equity, off-balance for 30/06/2026, files last saved 13/07/2026).
4. RBI Group Q2-2026 disclosure (31/07/2026) — both the results presentation and, decisively, the 'Q2 Results Internet' .xlsm databook, whose dedicated SEE-RS worksheet was parsed cell-by-cell. This is the group-level reconciliation the baseline flagged as never done: RBI's own SEE-RS sheet gives Serbia 104 business outlets against 103 branches in the bank's locator — the two agree, so the country figure is now reconciled to a group disclosure.
5. Regulator — National Bank of Serbia acceptance-network statistics (prihvatna_mreza.xlsx), refreshed 19/08/2026, giving Q2-2026 ATM and POS counts. This SUPERSEDES the baseline's Q1-2026 figure.

WHAT CHANGED VS THE 30/07/2026 BASELINE:
- NBS Serbia acceptance network moved from 3,336 ATMs / 187,957 POS (Q1-2026) to 3,412 ATMs / 195,121 POS (Q2-2026). Serbia's ATM fleet is growing, not shrinking.
- The '1m-client target' is resolved and is behind the bank, not ahead: 1,175,109 customers at 30/06/2026 per RBI's own databook.
- A Serbian bank resolution-fund levy appears for the first time in 2026 (EUR 4.58m booked in H1, ~EUR 8m expected for the full year for this bank alone).
- Serbia entered SEPA on 05/05/2026, SCT scheme only, all Serbian banks as indirect participants.
- Six Global Finance corporate digital awards announced 24/08/2026 — three days before this run.

GENUINE GAPS (and why):
- 'x-core incumbency (Bank Yourself)': not corroborated anywhere in the bank's own primary materials. Reported as an explicit negative finding for the Orchestrator to adjudicate rather than silently dropped.
- ATM/recycler HARDWARE VENDOR for Raiffeisen Serbia's 417 devices is not disclosed in any primary source opened. There is no Serbian equivalent of the NCR Atleos page that names Printec at BCR Romania.
- Installed POS terminal COUNT for the bank specifically is not disclosed — the annual report gives growth rates (POS +32%, e-commerce +44%, RaiPOS tap-to-phone +90%) but no absolute base. NBS publishes only the market total.
- Serbian-language press and any H1-2026 local-media interviews could not be swept: this session's WebSearch budget was fully exhausted (200/200) before the first query for this bank, and every curl-based search fallback was blocked (see access_issues). All findings here are therefore from sources reached by direct URL, which biases coverage toward the bank's own site, RBI IR and NBS, and away from journalism and third-party vendor announcements.
- NBS quarterly banking-sector report for Q2-2026 could not be located: the listing page renders its document list via JavaScript and direct filename guessing against the documents-eng/kontrola-banaka path returned no 200s.
access_issues:
1. WebSearch: hard budget exhaustion. The session had already used 200/200 WebSearch calls before this bank's first query, so ZERO keyword searching was available for this target. Logged rather than worked around silently.
2. Search-engine fallbacks over curl, all attempted with a desktop Chrome User-Agent:
   - html.duckduckgo.com/html/ -> HTTP 202 anti-bot interstitial, no results. BLOCKED.
   - lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/ -> HTTP 202, same. BLOCKED.
   - mojeek.com -> HTTP 200 but a JavaScript CAPTCHA challenge page, then HTTP 403 'your network appears to be sending automated queries'. BLOCKED.
   - searx.be -> HTTP 200 but empty result body. BLOCKED.
   - priv.au -> HTTP 429. BLOCKED.
   - bing.com -> HTTP 200 and parseable, the only one that worked, but it returned only brand-navigational results (mostly raiffeisen.ro and raiffeisen.ch) and nothing usable for Serbia. Effectively USELESS for this beat.
3. Claude-in-Chrome escalation ATTEMPTED as the rules require, after the fallbacks failed: the extension reported 'Claude in Chrome is not connected' — not installed or not signed in in this environment. So the prescribed escalation path was unavailable.
4. www.raiffeisenbank.rs/api/locations -> HTTP 404. Route found instead via the AEM component path in the locations page HTML (documented in coverage_notes).
5. nbs.rs/en/finansijske-institucije/platni-promet/statistika/ -> HTTP 404 (stale path). Working NBS statistics path reached via nbs.rs/en/ciljevi-i-funkcije/platni-sistem/statistika/.
6. nbs.rs/en/ciljevi-i-funkcije/finansijska-stabilnost/restrukturiranje-banaka/ -> HTTP 404. The legal basis for the new 2026 Serbian resolution-fund levy therefore could NOT be traced to an NBS primary page; that signal rests on RBI's booked charge only and is flagged for follow-up.
7. NBS quarterly banking-sector report list renders via JavaScript; direct filename probing of documents-eng/kontrola-banaka/ for I/II 2026 returned no 200s.
8. .../izvestaji/2026/podaci-i-informacije-o-banci/podaci-i-informacije-o-banci-30-06-2026.pdf -> HTTP 404: the H1-2026 Pillar-3 disclosure is not yet published at the path the 2025 editions use. Worth re-probing in September.
9. PDFs were extracted LOCALLY with pdfminer.six rather than through the fetch tool, per the access rules.
operator_requests:
1. NOT a paywall issue but the single biggest constraint this run: WebSearch was exhausted (200/200) and every curl search fallback is bot-blocked, while Claude-in-Chrome is not connected. An operator should either raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION, stagger banks across sessions, or connect the Chrome extension. Without one of these, Serbian-language press and vendor announcements are structurally unreachable for this beat.
2. Please have an operator run a plain web search for the exact phrases "Bank Yourself" and "x-core" together with Raiffeisen / Serbia / bankomat. I could not corroborate either from primary sources and I want to know whether the brief item is real, belongs to a different bank, or should be retired.
3. Vendor identification request: find who supplies and services (a) Raiffeisen Serbia's 417 ATMs, especially the 206 EUR-capable multifunction units, and (b) the 'Kuan' and 'Livix' merchant cash-deposit terminals installed at 34 and 14 branches respectively. Vendor press releases and case-study pages are exactly what search would surface and I could not reach them.
4. Re-probe in September 2026 for the H1-2026 'Podaci i informacije o banci' Pillar-3 disclosure, which was not yet at its usual path.
5. Trace the Serbian legal instrument that introduced the bank resolution fund levy effective 2026 (NBS or Official Gazette); the NBS bank-resolution page 404s.
